sections.h2: How Michigan handles unpaid property taxes
sections.html:
Michigan moves delinquent parcels through forfeiture to the county treasurer and then a court foreclosure. The General Property Tax Act, MCL 211.78 and following, then provides for a sale or transfer of the foreclosed parcel under section 78m.

For an owner, the practical meaning is a fixed calendar. Taxes go delinquent, the parcel forfeits, a circuit court enters a foreclosure judgment, and redemption rights end on a set date after that judgment. Until that date the owner, or anyone with a legal interest in the property, can pay the redemption amount and stop the process.

That calendar is also the window in which a sale of the house can solve the problem, because a buyer's closing funds can pay the county treasurer before title passes to the government.

sections.h2: When a Michigan property forfeits for unpaid tax
sections.html:
On March 1 of each tax year, property that has been delinquent for taxes, interest, penalties and fees for the immediately preceding 12 months or more is forfeited to the county treasurer, along with certified abandoned property. That rule is in MCL 211.78g(1).

The treasurer adds a $175 fee to each forfeited parcel. Within 45 days after forfeiture the treasurer records a certificate with the register of deeds stating that the property has been forfeited and not redeemed, and that absolute title will vest in the foreclosing governmental unit on the March 31 after a foreclosure judgment. The certificate must also explain a former owner's right to claim any remaining proceeds after a sale.

A county treasurer must withhold a property from forfeiture for any reason the State Tax Commission sets by rule.

sections.h2: How long you have to redeem
sections.html:
Redemption is open until the March 31 after the circuit court enters a judgment of foreclosure. In a contested case, it ends 21 days after the judgment. The judge must enter the judgment no later than March 30 following the hearing (MCL 211.78k(5)).

To redeem, pay the county treasurer the full amount of unpaid delinquent taxes, interest, penalties and fees. Add interest at a noncompounded 1/2 percent per month, or fraction of a month, on the taxes originally returned as delinquent, counted from the March 1 before forfeiture, along with recording fees and the cost of serving notices. The treasurer may waive that extra interest when the property is withheld from the foreclosure petition under section 78h(3)(c).

Michigan tax foreclosure calendar for a forfeited parcel
StepTiming
Forfeiture to county treasurerMarch 1, after 12 or more months delinquent
Certificate of forfeiture recordedWithin 45 days after forfeiture
Judgment of foreclosure enteredNo later than the following March 30
Redemption ends, uncontested caseMarch 31 after the judgment
Redemption ends, contested case21 days after the judgment

sections.h2: What happens at the foreclosure hearing?
sections.html:
A person with an interest in a listed parcel may contest the forfeited taxes by filing written objections with the circuit court clerk and serving the foreclosing governmental unit before the hearing date. The grounds are narrow:

  • No law authorizes the tax.
  • The body that decides whether to levy a tax acted without jurisdiction or never imposed the tax.
  • The property was exempt, or the tax was not legally levied.
  • The tax was paid within the time allowed.
  • The tax was assessed fraudulently.
  • The property description was so vague or wrong that the forfeiture was void.

The court may also hold a property out of foreclosure for one year, or extend the redemption period, if the owner is a minor heir, is incompetent, is without means of support, or faces substantial financial hardship. A taxing unit's lien is not harmed by that delay, and the parcel returns to the next year's proceeding.

sections.h2: What the foreclosure judgment does to the title
sections.html:
If nothing is paid by the redemption deadline, fee simple title vests absolutely in the foreclosing governmental unit. The judgment extinguishes all liens against the property, including tax and special assessment liens, apart from future special assessment installments and certain state environmental liens. It also ends every recorded and unrecorded interest, with exceptions for visible or recorded easements, private deed restrictions, certain oil and gas interests and a few others.

After that date the judgment generally cannot be modified, stayed or held invalid. Appeals go to the Court of Appeals on the circuit court record, and a person appealing must pay the county treasurer the amount found due by the deadline, with the notice of appeal. If the foreclosure is affirmed, the money is refunded.

If a property is redeemed, the treasurer issues a redemption certificate, and one copy is recorded with the register of deeds. Unpaid taxes that were never returned as delinquent are not extinguished by that redemption.

sections.h2: Payment plans and reductions for owner-occupants
sections.html:
These exist for a principal residence that is exempt from the school operating tax. Under MCL 211.78q, a foreclosing governmental unit may offer a delinquent property tax installment plan to a financially distressed owner, and a county treasurer may sign a tax foreclosure avoidance agreement of up to 5 years for residential property once the owner makes an initial payment the treasurer sets.

  • While an agreement is in effect, the property is withheld from the foreclosure petition and interest runs at 1/2 percent per month, noncompounded, counted from the date the taxes were originally returned as delinquent, in place of the extra interest counted from March 1.
  • A treasurer may not sign more than 2 agreements with the same owner.
  • If the owner defaults, the extra interest applies and the parcel goes into the next foreclosure petition.

Participating local units may also adopt a payment reduction program described in MCL 211.78g(8). Ask the county treasurer which of these programs the county offers, since each county decides what it makes available.

sections.h2: Claiming money after a tax foreclosure sale
sections.html:
A person who held a legal interest just before the foreclosure judgment took effect can claim the remaining proceeds from a later sale. The amount is what the sale brought in, minus the minimum bid, the other costs of the forfeiture, foreclosure, sale and upkeep, and a 5 percent sale commission (MCL 211.78t).

The process runs in two steps:

  • By July 1 after the foreclosure takes effect, send the foreclosing governmental unit a notarized notice on the Treasury form, by personal service or certified mail.
  • After receiving the unit's notice, file a motion with the circuit court during the window from February 1 to May 15 following the sale or transfer.

The claimant carries the burden of proof, and the right cannot be transferred except by will or intestate succession. Calendar both dates as soon as the foreclosure is effective.

sections.h2: Why sell before the foreclosure judgment?
sections.html:
Once the judgment is effective, the owner loses the house and every equity dollar in it, except what a successful remaining-proceeds claim returns after the government sells. A sale before the redemption deadline can pay the treasurer's payoff figure at closing and leave the seller with the difference.

Ask the county treasurer for a written payoff that includes interest, fees and recording costs, and for a redemption certificate once the money is paid. Confirm with the register of deeds that the certificate is recorded. If the redemption deadline is close, tell the title company at the start so the wire and recording steps fit before it.

A cash sale suits this situation because the buyer does not wait on a lender's appraisal or underwriting. The closing agent pays the treasurer from the proceeds, you receive what is left, and the foreclosure stops. Bring the parcel number, the latest tax statement and any notices you received from the county treasurer or the court.

faqs.q: Does Michigan sell tax lien certificates to investors?
faqs.a: The unpaid-tax statutes provide for forfeiture to the county treasurer and a court foreclosure, followed by a sale or transfer under MCL 211.78m. Ask the county treasurer how the county handles foreclosed parcels.
It is the March 31 after the judgment of foreclosure, or 21 days after the judgment in a contested case. The county treasurer can confirm the date for your parcel.

faqs.q: What is the extra fee on a forfeited property?
faqs.a: The county treasurer adds $175 to each forfeited property. Redemption also adds 1/2 percent per month, noncompounded, on the originally delinquent taxes from the March 1 before forfeiture.

faqs.q: Can I still claim money if the county sells my foreclosed house?
faqs.a: You may. A person with a legal interest just before the judgment can claim remaining proceeds, starting with a notice due by July 1 after the foreclosure takes effect and a court motion filed between February 1 and May 15.

faqs.q: Can the court delay a foreclosure for hardship?
faqs.a: Yes. For a minor heir, an incompetent owner, an owner without means of support or one in substantial financial hardship, the court may hold the property out for one year or extend the redemption period.
